items.title: Observability
items.description:
This course covers the fundamentals of observability in distributed systems. Today, Kubernetes has become the de facto standard for Cloud Native applications and is widely used for distributed systems. To be effective as an observability expert, it is critical to understand how to monitor and respond to the health and performance of both your Kubernetes clusters and the applications hosted on them. This course will teach students how to collect system performance data using Prometheus, how to collect application tracing data using Jaeger, and how to visualize the results in a dashboard using Grafana.Introduction to Cloud Observability
In this first lesson, we'll go over the big picture. Why is observability relevant? And what is your role is as an observability engineer? What tools will you need to be able to conduct observability?
 Observability Tools
This lesson will get you set up with Prometheus, Jaeger, and Grafana, the main tools you need to start doing observability in your cluster.
 SLOs, SLIs, and Error Budgets
In order to observe performance, we first need to get clear on how we are defining and measuring it. We'll do this using Service-Level Objectives and Service-Level Indicators.
 Tracing
Tracing will allow us to get performance data on our applications, particularly on the latency of the key processes within them. In this lesson, we'll learn how to conduct tracing using Jaeger.
 Building Dashboards
We'll look at how we can use Grafana to visualize the data we've been collecting, so that we can see the performance of our system and application at a glance.

items.title: Applying AI to 2D Medical Imaging Data
items.description:
Introduction to AI for 2D Medical Imaging
In this lesson, you will be given an introduction to this course about AI for 2D medical imaging, why AI is important and where AI fits in the space.
 Clinical Foundations of 2D Medical Imaging
In this lesson, we will cover clinical foundations such as clinical workflows, applications of 2D imaging in clinical settings and how machine learning impacts clinics.
 2D Medical Imaging Exploratory Data Analysis
In this lesson, we will learn the DICOM standard in medical imaging, and how to explore medical imaging data and prepare it for machine learning applications.
 Classification Models of 2D Medical Images
In this lesson, we'll dive deep into classification tasks for 2D medical imaging using different machine learning models. and we will talk about pre-process data, train, test, and validate models.
 Translating AI Algorithms for Clinical Settings with the FDA
In this lesson, you will learn about how your work fits into the bigger picture, and how it’s regulated by the FDA, which is an often-overlooked, but incredibly important.

items.title: Applying AI to 3D Medical Imaging Data
items.description:
Introduction to AI for 3D Medical Imaging
In this lesson, we will introduce the course and instructors. We will give you an overview of the context for AI in 3D medical imaging space, and cover the objectives of the course.
 3D Medical Imaging - Clinical Fundamentals
In this lesson, we cover the basic terminology and concepts related to 3D medical imaging. We will look at the problem space from a clinical standpoint and learn how CT and MR scanners produce images.
 3D Imaging Exploratory Data Analysis
In this lesson, we will dive deeper into medical imaging formats NIFTI and DICOM, how scanner data is represented, and how to read medical volumes stored in these files and analyze them.
 3D Medical Imaging - End-to-End Deep Learning Applications
In this lesson, we cover the basics of building deep neural networks for 3D medical imaging (mostly segmentation & classification) and performance evaluation from a software and clinical perspective.
 Deploying AI Algorithms in Real World Scenarios
In this lesson, we'll talk about clinical networks, architecture, and AI deployment, tools and their use by data scientists and clinicians, as well as medical device regulation and data privacy.

items.title: Applying AI to EHR Data
items.description:
With the transition to electronic health records (EHR) over the last decade, the amount of EHR data has increased exponentially, providing an incredible opportunity to unlock this data with AI to benefit the healthcare system. Learn the fundamental skills of working with EHR data in order to build and evaluate compliant, interpretable machine learning models that account for bias and uncertainty using cutting-edge libraries and tools including Tensorflow Probability, Aequitas, and Shapley. Understand the implications of key data privacy and security standards in healthcare. Apply industry code sets, transform datasets at different EHR data levels, and use Tensorflow to engineer features.Applying AI to EHR Data Introduction
This lesson will provide you with an Introduction to the EHR Data course outline, content, as well as introduce you to your instructor.
 EHR Data Security and Analysis
In this lesson, you will learn about the importance of data security and the different standards that apply to EHR, as well as analyzing EHR data.
 EHR Code Sets
In this lesson you will learn how to work with different EHR codes and how to map them properly to records.
 EHR Transformations & Feature Engineering
In this lesson, you'll gain skills in feature engineering and transformation of EHR.
 Building, Evaluating and Interpreting Models
In this final lesson, you'll be putting all of your skills together to build, evaluate and interpret ML models for Bias and Uncertainty.

items.title: Applying AI to Wearable Device Data
items.description:
Introduction to Wearable Data
We’ll cover what wearables are and the scope of the class. Learn who your instructor is and his thoughts on the promise and caveats of wearables in medical research and decision making.
 Intro to Digital Sampling & Signal Processing
A brief tour through sampling theory, signal processing, the Fourier transform, and other related topics. We’ll briefly cover some plotting and visualization techniques here as well.
 Introduction to Sensors
We cover the basics of the accelerometer, the PPG sensor, and the ECG sensor, as well as what these signals look like in typical environments and the types of noise that we will encounter.
 Activity Classification
Build an activity classifier using a wrist-worn accelerometer!
 ECG Signal Processing
We deep dive into a fundamental algorithm for ECG processing and use that as the basis for an arrhythmia detection algorithm.

This module  deals with the important nutrients  required by plants and their functions. Nutrient  deficiencies may result in negative impacts on plants. There is  the involvement  of numerous factors  that make these nutrients available  tp plants. These include  enviromental  conditions ,  microorganisms  and soil organisms. Nutrients  are recycled. Important  nutrient  cycles,  include nitrogen ,  sulphur  and carbon  cycles. The water  cycle  is also important  through  water is not considered  as plant nutrient . Nutrients  need to be measured  in the soil ,  water and atmosphere  and other  abiotic  factors. Enviromental  impacts  with excessive  use of nutrients . These are important  to determine the health status  of plants  via the measurement of nutrients  in the enviroment. Other parameters  include pH and conductivity . These are important  to adjust  the amount of nutrients  required  by plants.
1. The elements and their relationship  to plants  2. Soil - plant - atmosphere  distribution of nutrients  3. Use of nutrients  with minimal harmful effects on the enviroment. 1. Apply the best method to work out simple work related calculations in relation to volume and area. Demonsrate proper use of equations and formulas so as to ensure effective cleaning. Build confidence when using heavy duty cleaning machines. Use the correct cleaning tools according to the task at hand. Apply the correct cleaning approach according to the industry requirements. Demonstrate confidence in knowing the correct cleaning procedure to be used.

items.title: Award in Assistant Limestone Block and Hollow Concrete Block Layer
items.description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety working practices; acquire knowledge to be able to assist in the identification of systems,  equipment and components; develop knowledge and skills to be able to assist in reading of drawings and calculations with approved procedures and under supervision; and to be knowledgeable and have the skill of assisting in the laying of limestone and hollow concrete blocks to line.
Assist in the identification of systems,  equipment and components. Assist in reading of drawings and calculations. Communicate with fellow workers. Read method statements and safe works preventive measures. Apply occupational health and safety during work practices. Assist in the  laying of limestone and hollow concrete blocks to line. Implement actions as per method statements and safe work practices

items.title: Award in Customer Care
items.description:
The course addresses  the significant need of customer care aptitude in the current economic situation which  stresses excellence in customer care  service
Knowledge,  Skills and Competences  At the end of the course the learner is expected to demonstrate basic competency in Customer Care skills with some independence and autonomy. This will include: Knowledge:  a)Being aware and responsive to the policies and procedures of the specific work area. b)Appreciating the role of internal customers. c)Measure the service against that of competitors. Skills: a)Offering the best possible service to customers in a professional manner.  b)Exhibiting good listening skills to understand the customers’ needs. c)Working as part of a team in order to provide the customer with the best possible service. d)Using appropriate telephone techniques e)Developing effective communication skills to succeed in Customer Service.  Competences: a)Practicing empathy and assertiveness when problem solving. b)Being competent in dealing with customers’ complaints. c)Show competence in dealing with angry customersd)Continuously collect feedback from customers to improve service

items.title: VET Award  Foundation in Oxy Acetylene Welding and Cutting
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to gain employment as an Oxy-Acetylene Welder. Through this training programme,  the learner will review OHS requirements for welding environments and be able select suitable techniques to produce basic welded joints including Gas Cutting using Oxy-Acetylene welding technology.
Quote health and safety principles and regulations for working with Oxy-Acetylene Welding equipment. Describe health and safety measures and precautions to prevent hazards and to ensure the safety of oneself and third parties when working with Oxy-Acetylene Welding equipment. Describe the procedures and processes to weld beads on a steel plate in the flat position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding. Describe the procedures and processes to weld Lap Fillet Joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding. Demonstrate knowledge of typical basic non destructive testing procedures used by the industry to check welds. Use industry standard techniques to check a weld for visual defeats. Practice welding Tee Fillet Joints in the flat position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding. Practice welding Tee Fillet Joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding.

items.title: Award as Assistant Tile Layer
Fire Safety and Related Emergencies
items.description:
This course is designed to raise awareness on fire hazards and train participants on how to act safely in the event of an emergency fire situation.
A sound understanding of the role,  functions and responsibility of a fire marshal; Ability to identify which are the elements that need to be present for a fire to occurs,  the three basic principles of fire extinction and the principles and practice of fire risk analysis; Ability to identify the key elements for effective fire risk management in the workplace; Knowledge of the use of various types of fire equipment; An understanding of the correct methods of fire prevention measures that can be taken to minimize fire hazards; Knowledge of common types of evacuation procedures and the control of personnel; Knowledge of all categories of fire signage,  according to the type of message they are intended to convey Follow fire prevention good practices; Determine the type of approach needed to properly apply fire safety procedures for every workplace; Understand the importance of teamwork in an emergency situation; Apply fire control measures to manage fire inherent and residual risks; Cooperate with co-workers and health & safety representatives in the event of an emergency in any workplace. Adequately apply organisational & prioritizing skills in emergency situations. Identify and be able to use fire fighting equipment (extinguishers,  hydrants fire signage,  smoke alarms fire blanket and personal fire protection equipment). Instruct personnel to prevent basic and arson fire prevention. Observe,  receive and obtain information to complete an incident report form. Implement risk analysis in the workplace and be able to manage these risks. Implement measures to protect all workers,  colleagues and clients. Identify the safety fire equipment available and manage the safe use of portable fire-fighting equipment. Manage emergency procedures and the control of personnel

items.title: Award in Authorised Gas Tester
items.description:
The course will provide the learner with a brief background  to the requirements of the Gas testing procedure and confined space entry procedure.  Provide the necessary understanding of the basics of hazard management of oxygen enriched/ deficient,  toxic and flammable gas atmospheres.  It will enhance the learners competency and ability to identify atmospheres that me be immediately dangerous to life or health.
The learner will be able to: To furthers ones knowledge on the use of portable gas tester; To furtherones knowledge on air testing; To further ones knowledge on the use of portable gas tester; To develop the use of relevent information and furhter knowledge in practical skills when analysing air in a confined space; Understand the narcotic effects of hydrocarbons; To furhter ones knowledge in gas testing for hot work and confined spaces. The learner will be able to:  Effective use of a portable gas monitor to test and area and to Interpret and document the results of gas testing.

items.title: Award in Assistant Demolition Operative
items.description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with sound knowledge of occupational health and safety working practices and acquire the competence to be able to assist to operate handheld power tools and equipment in the workplace within the building and construction sector. The candidate shall cover procedures and principles on how to assist in demolition and dismantling of existing structures manually (by hand) under supervision on construction sites.
Learning to learn how to keep updated with the content learned during the course. Communicate with colleagues and supervisors or site managers. Communicate using simple glossary terms used in the building and construction. Communicate using basic Maltese or English. Use appropriate nonverbal communication

items.title: Award in Health and Safety at the Workplace
items.description:
Aimed at providing basic knowledge to health and safety, including minimizing risk of injury, accident prevention, and other ways to improve safety at the workcation and support on construction sites.
The learner will be able to: 

- Ability to understand, interpret and apply health and safety regulation.
- Assess risk and provide consultancy on mitigating it.
- Lead individuals to a healthier and safer environment through consultancy and raising awareness of health and safety on 
  construction sites.
- Provide health and safety reports.
- Resolve disputes and improve the work environment. The learner will be able to: 

- Prevent health and safety hazards
- Understand better work environment
-Use of health and safety equipment
- Appropriately manage incidents at work place The learner will be able to: 

- Provide insight in the health and safety report
- Train on how to approach individuals who require health and safety support
- Report writing
- Basic knowledge of fire and first aid.

items.title: Award in Common Health and Safety Issues: Occupational Risk for Lone Workers,  Young Workers and Workers in Hot and Cold Environments
items.description:
The course is designed to provide participants with the knowledge and awareness of specific hazards at workplace: heat and cold stress (temperature at which work becomes dangerous),  lone working (a person who works alone) and safety risks for young worker (a person under eighteen years of age who works).
Report properly all accidents,  injuries,  near-misses and other dangerous occurrences. Identify correct health and safety procedures connected with the type of working practice when someone is working alone. An understanding of the importance of personal safety for lone workers. Knowledge of the risks that a person may face as a lone worker and ways to reduce these risks. An understanding of how cooperate among workers to improve safety and health’ procedures in circumstances involving lone labours.

items.title: Award in Basic Tile Laying Techniques
items.description:
The training course is intended to give the necessary knowledge, skills and competences to someone wishing to work in the building and construction sector. It is specifically focusing on basic tile laying knowledge and skills.
Outline the preventative and remedial actions to be taken in the case of exposure to materials hazardous to health. Report any hazards which may present risk to relevant persons. Assist and perform installation of tiles under supervision. Confirm that all materials, tools and equipment necessary for the installation process are available as required. Confirm that all material, tools and equipment are fit for their intended purpose. Understand and explain the correct procedure for setting out work systems. Identify instances where additional information would be necessary and liaise with supervisor accordingly. Look for information, directions and guidance in the use of materials and tools

items.title: Award in Provision  for Cleaning Services
items.description:
This course is specifically designed taking into account the limitations of persons employed in the industry in terms of learning capabilities and an extremely interactive approach shall be undertaken,  with the trainer having been involved in the cleaning industry for years and owning one of the major cleaning companies in Malta. To this effect,  the students shall be embracing first-hand experience with regards to both the theoratical aspect of the course and with continuous hands-on experience reflecting the theoretical parts of the course.
1. Be conversant with the basic theoratical and practical aspects of health and safety in the cleaning industry 2. Attain basic knowledge of chemical handling 3. Identify the correct to use of cleaning machinery  4. Recognise  the importance of COSHH regulations (Control Substances Hazardous to Health) 5. Show an understanding of the use of colour codes 6. Understand the problems with cross contamination 7. Be proficient in the understanding of the difference between cleaning,  disinfection and decontamination 8. Recognise the importance of correct storage of equipment and machinery. 1. Perform general duties relating to cleaning 2. Follow good working practise in relation to use of equipment and machinery 3. Determine the type of approach needed with regards to cleaning,  disinfection and decontamination 4. Access or request to all sources of information relating to COSHH regulations (Control of Subsances Hazardous to Health). 5. Provide suitable solutions for avoidance of cross contamination 6. Follow good working practices relating to correct storage of equipment and machinery 7. Access or request to sources of information relating to colour codes 8.Follow good working practices with regards to chemical handling 9. Establish clients requirements in such a manner that bridges the relationship between the employer and the client 10. Communicate and maintain a dialogue with the supervisors at work when necessary and on an ongoing basis 11. Assess which work practice is the most adequate in terms of health and safety  12. Learn both  the theoratical and practical necessities for performing the job description correctly.

items.title: Award in Waste Collection and Transportation of Waste
items.description:
Transport and disposal of municipal solid waste is one of the major environmental problems. Improper transport and disposal of municipal solid waste causes hazards to inhabitants. The amount of solid waste generated is steadily increasing and every government in this world is currently focusing on methods to approach the challenge. This unit develops good awareness of recycling activities and key statutory requirements. In addition,  learners will be more skilled at organising their workspace,  working practices and resources as well as working more effectively with each other as a team. Overall,  they will acquire the skills necessary to work more safely and efficiently.
Understand ways of mitigating potential impacts during the collection and transport of waste. Environmental Impact of Waste Management. Regulatory Policy and Legislation. Understanding the principles and procedures for waste transfer activities. Identify types of waste and arising in the Maltese Islands and relevant stakeholders. Health and Safety in the collection and handling of waste.

items.title: Award in Safe Use of Electrical Hand Held Apparatus
items.description:
This course is designed for those workers who need to work on electrical equipment who either have no electrical qualifications or need a reminder of electrical dangers and safe working practices. This course provides knowledge and skills on electrical and mechanical hazards,  on the functioning of portable tools and on the safety procedures to use at workplace.
Perform a basic risk assessment to identify the hazards specific to electrical safety,  the risks arising from those hazards,  and the control measures you should use.Achieve a visual inspection that should be carried out by the user each and every time the equipment is used,  checking for example for evidence of damage,  loose cables etc. Determine the type of approach needed to comply with safe work procedure. Apply procedures of operational maintenance. Cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives in the organisation of an electrical emergency in workplace. Know the general site safety,  particularly from the point of view of electrical hazards. Understand the electrical and mechanical hazards that can be encountered using an electrical tool and the precautions to be taken. Know technical and organisational preventive measures relevant to electrical and mechanical hazards in the use of electrical hand held apparatus. Know how identify and report faulty portable electrical equipment and withdraw it from service,  by ensuring it cannot be used and/or is marked faulty.

items.title: Award in Health and Safety
items.description:
The aim of this module is to provide learners with the basic health and safety knowledge and skill requirements
The learner will be able to: a) Understand health and safety requirementsb) Identify risks and hazards The Elements of the law Advantages and disadvantages of the law History of occupational health and safety Hazards caused by fire Learning the recovery position Treatment to chocking Treatment to electrical shock Sprains and strains First aid box Electrical safety Classes of fire and fire extinguishers Safety signs Health and Safety responsibilities of the employer Powers of officers

items.title: Foundation Certificate in Applied Science
items.description:
This programme of studies is aimed at giving learners the opportunity to further their studies in several diverse sciencerelated areas including environmental,  health and industrial sciences. Learners will cover various topics such as Chemistry,  Physics,  Biology,  English,  Maltese,  Mathematics and IT which will be taught in an applied manner that is relevant to the various science sectors in which employment may be sought with a higher qualification. This programme is particularly suitable for learners who have a scientific or technical aptitude,  even if they have not decided fully on their ultimate career choice.
Understand some of the factors that influence scientific progress. Describe the main factors that affect the health of individuals Make accurate scientific observations and measurements in given situations Understand what skills and qualities are required for jobs in the science sector
